meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas. doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: mTORC2 puts the second, activating phosphate on Akt (Ser473). This is the step rapamycin eventually breaks, and a major reason, in mice, that chronic rapamycin impairs glucose tolerance (LAM2012).
data.mechanism_beginner: mTORC2 adds the final activating tag to Akt – the same step that long-term use of the drug rapamycin eventually disrupts. In mice, that disruption is a major reason long-term rapamycin raises blood sugar.
data.context: S473 contribution to Akt output is substrate-dependent: some Akt substrates are strongly mTORC2-dependent, others barely.
data.note: Bridge edge between the growth-factor route and the rapamycin route.
